until they hibernate.
* A scheduled eval that hits the budget pauses its schedule rather than
retrying into the same cap every window; it resumes once you raise the cap or
the period rolls over.
* Runs that use **your own API keys** are never counted against the budget and
never blocked by it. Neither is the free daily allowance, which is not
credits.
* The window is your organization's own billing period: the subscription cycle
for team and enterprise plans, and the calendar month otherwise. Raising or
lowering the cap mid-period does not reset what has already been spent.
Any member can see the budget and how much of it is left; only owners and
admins can change it. Every change is recorded in the organization's audit log
with who made it and what it was before.
The same budget is readable and writable from the API at
`/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/spend-budget`.
### Managing billing details
Organization owners on a paid plan see a **Manage billing** button on the billing page. Clicking it opens the Stripe portal where
you can update payment methods, download invoices, add tax IDs, and review billing details. Only organization owners can access th
is portal.

781:### Provider quota
783:`provider/quota`
785:Your LLM provider rejected the request because you hit a rate limit or quota. This is a limit on your own provider key; no MCP
Jam purchase lifts it.
789:* Per-minute rate limit exceeded.
790:* Daily or monthly quota exhausted.
791:* Free tier limits hit.
795:* Wait for the limit window to reset, then retry.
799:> **MCPJam account limit vs. provider throttle.** If the session pane shows a billing or credit message instead of this card,
the limit is on your MCPJam account, not your provider key. Adding credits or switching to BYOK resolves that case; the steps abov
e do not apply.
814:* Click **Not now** to dismiss and continue with a standard model. Your credit balance is not affected.

start the run; start a new run once credits are available.

919:### Server rate limited
921:`server/rate_limited`
923:The MCP server rejected the request with HTTP 429 (too many requests). This is the server's own limit, not your LLM provider's
; see [Provider quota](#provider-quota) for that case.
927:* The server enforces its own per-client rate limit.
